title: Long Division: Dividing up to 4-Digit Numbers by 1-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Long Division Worksheets: 4-Digit by 1-Digit (TEKS 4.4E, 4.4F, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.4E represent the quotient of up to a four-digit whole number divided by a one-digit whole number using arrays, area models, or equations; 4.4F use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to divide up to a four-digit dividend by a one-digit divisor
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 long division worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.4E and 4.4F: divide using facts, area models and equations, 2- to 4-digit dividends, zeros in the quotient and remainders. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_sub: Write 0 in the quotient when a place cannot be divided. The remainder is less than the divisor.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Divide from the greatest place: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat.
  • If a place cannot be divided, write 0 in the quotient.
  • The remainder must be less than the divisor.
  • Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend.

Examples

Example

2,436 ÷ 6

24 hundreds ÷ 6 = 4 hundreds.

3 tens ÷ 6 = 0 tens (write 0).

36 ones ÷ 6 = 6.

Answer: 406

Example

Check 125 ÷ 4 = 31 R1

31 × 4 = 124

124 + 1 = 125

Answer: correct

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out a 0 in the quotient: 2,436 ÷ 6 = 46Write 0 when a place cannot be divided.
A remainder as big as the divisorIf the remainder is too big, the quotient digit is too small.
Forgetting to bring down a digitBring down one digit at a time.

The amount left over when a number cannot be divided equally. It is always less than the divisor.

faq.q: How do I check a division answer?
faq.a: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder. You should get the dividend.

items.e: 4,200 is 42 hundreds. 42 ÷ 7 = 6, so 42 hundreds ÷ 7 = 6 hundreds = 600. Check: 600 × 7 = 4,200.
